ANOOP CHITKARA, J.

 37 13.02.2024 Chhappar, District 406, 420, 506 IPC, 1860  Yamuna Nagar

Seeking quashing of the FIR captioned above, the accused-petitioners have come up before this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
2.

To ascertain that whether the present petition is worth issuing notices or not, I have heard counsel for the petitioners and have gone through the pleadings and its analysis would lead to following outcome.

sentences.text:
FIR has been annexed as Annexure P-1 which reads as follows:
"Mr. Superintendent of Police, Yamunanagar Subject: application regarding taking appropriate Legal action against: -1 - Sukhwinder Singh son of Shri Gurbachan Singh, 2 Darneet Singh S/o Sukhwinder Singh residents village Milksukhi, Post Office Mandhar Tehsil Jagadhri District Yamuna Nagar, and to register a case for committing fraud, cheating and by misleading sold Land and swindled money,
thereafter giving threats to kill and implicate in false cases.

Sir, the complainant makes the following request: That according to Jamabadi year 2019- 20 accused no.1 Sukhvinder Singh is owner in possession of 11 Kanla 1 Marla land out of total land 20 Kanal 16 Marla in Khasra number-13/15, 16, 14/11, 20, 21/1, situated in village Milksukhi Tehsil Jagadhri District Yamunanagar.
And the accused had told that ownership of this land is in his name and there is no dispute or litigation regarding this land and said that he wants to sell this land further.

That the said accused no.1 agreed to sell 8 Kanal 0 Marla land from Khasra number-13//15, 16,
14//11, 20, 21/1 vide agreement to sell date 05-03-2022 for 33,00,000/- and vide agreement dated 05-03-2022 accused no.1 has received from me the complainant 10,00,000/- in presence of witnesses, out of which 1 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:093705 CRM-M-52212-2023 23,50,000/- was paid in cash and 26,50,000/- was paid by cheque number-182120 of Union Bank of India.

And 05-09-2022 was fixed as date of registration deed and after receiving the earnest money accused no.1 had signed the agreement and receipt as the seller and the witnesses also signed on the agreement and this agreement was got attested by notary public by both the parties. 2- That at the time of making the agreement the accused told that the said land is mortgaged with Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank Harnauli and this was also agreed that the accused will be bound to get redeemed the said land before the date of registration deed and accused no.1 will obtain NOC etc.
from the bank at his own expense and will be bound to get registered the deed in the name of the complainant on the fixed date and this was also decided that the accused at the time of registration of registration deed would hand over the possession of the area of 0 Kanal 13 Marla to the complainant out of their Khasra number 14/11(7-7)
and Khasra No. 14//20

and before handing over the possession the accused will get this area measured at their own expense and will hand over the possession of the entire area to the complainant."
4. A perusal of the aforesaid FIR clearly mentions that at the time of agreement the accused-petitioner no.1 submitted that he would clear the mortgages from Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank Harnauli.
The said fact is also clear from the perusal of the FIR and agreement to sell which have been annexed as Annexure P-2 and Annexure P-3 which is an affidavit of petitioner No.1-Sukhwinder Singh.

5. The counsel for the petitioner submits that at the time of agreement he had told the purchaser about the mortgage of the land with Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank Harnauli and purchaser had undertaken to purchase the said land subject to redemption.

sentences.text: A perusal of the agreement Annexure P-2 also mentions that the property is mortgaged with Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank Harnauli and the seller would redeem the mortgage at his own expenditure and except that there is no other incumberance on it.

7. Before registration of the FIR dated 13.02.2024, the petitioner had sent a legal notice to the respondent Nos.2 and 3 i.e. purchaser through his counsel on 11.12.2023 which is annexed as Annexure P-5.
In the said notice, it has been mentioned that the purchaser did not appear for the registration of sale deed.
On 31.08.2023, subsequently, date of execution of registration of sale deed was extended till 15.09.2023 and then accused remained present but the complainant did not come.
However, there is no mention in the legal notice about clearing of the mortgage.
Argument of the petitioners' counsel that it is a civil dispute is contradicted from the documents annexed by the petitioners themselves.

As per Annexure P-2, which is the agreement, clearly mentions that the property is under mortgage with Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank Harnauli and before the sale deed, the petitioner would get it redeemed at his own expenditure.
However, in the legal notice dated 11.12.2023 (Annexure P-5) the petitioners are silent about such redemption.
A perusal of the present quashing petition does not refer to any document which would corroborate the redemption from the bank being made or not.
2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:093705 CRM-M-25327-2024

The complainant's stand is that he has been duped by the petitioners despite of an undertaking to clear the redemption which was never done, thus, prima facie, the petitioner's malicious intent is writ at large in admitting the mention of mortgage in the agreement but after taking advance under this pretext, later on he did not redeem the mortgages.
Once they have taken the money from the purchaser, the redemption of the property from their side was not done which would clearly point out towards the intention to cheat.
Thus, the allegation clearly points out towards the malicious intent.
The petitioner's next argument is that the offences are under 406, 420 IPC cannot go side by side.
Regarding this matter the petitioner is permitted to take up all these points by filing a discharge application at appropriate stage.
However, it cannot be presumed that prosecution is being launched under Sections 406 and 420 IPC without justifying the maintainability of offences simultaneously.
Be that as it may, if that section survives FIR cannot be quashed.
7. In the entirety of the facts and circumstances and analysis of the above clearly points out that it is not a case worth issuing of notice.

The petitioner's contention that he wanted to perform his part of contract is also over to cover up the transfer of funds for the reasons that he never communicated about the redemption of mortgage which was primary incumberance without which the property cannot be transferred.
The property could not be transferred in favour of the purchaser because of the incumberance in the nature of mortgage.
8. Given above, the petition is dismissed in aforesaid terms.

(ANOOP CHITKARA)
